_comment: Committed result of `layout/erc/well_tap_audit.py` -- the direct
geometric answer to `does ADC_BLOCK draw well or substrate taps at
all?`, measured from the drawn layers with no implant marking, no
extraction deck and no net model involved (see ../README.md, issues
This file is BOTH the record and the expectation. `well_tap_audit.py`
re-derives every value under `measured` from the GDS named below and
fails if any of them moved, so the decision that rests on these
numbers (spec/decision-records/DR-0035-well-taps-and-tie-straps.md)
cannot be silently invalidated by a later layout edit.
THAT MECHANISM HAS ALREADY FIRED ONCE, WHICH IS THE POINT. This file
used to commit `well_tap_candidates: 0` and `metal1_label_texts: 0` on
both rings, and `sim/tests/test_well_tap_audit.py` pinned those zeros
by hand for DR-0032 (`implant layers stay undrawn until a well tap
exists to mark`). Issue #356 drew the taps; the audit and the test
went red; DR-0032 was SUPERSEDED by DR-0035 rather than re-baselined
quietly. The numbers below are the post-#356 state, and the test now
pins them in the other direction for the same reason.
HOW TO READ THE HEADLINE NUMBERS.
well_tap_candidates: 25, nwell_islands: 25
Of the 185 `COMP` 22/0 polygons that interact with an `Nwell`
21/0 island, 25 do NOT also interact with `Poly2` 30/0 -- one
per island. A diffusion region inside a well that is not part of
a transistor is a tap; the other 160 are transistor
source/drain/channel, the same 160 that were there before. Every
well in this block is tapped, and `lib/place.py` routes each tap
to the `vdd` trunk.
implant_layers_present: both true
`Nplus` 32/0 marks the 25 well taps and nothing else, which is
what makes the supply spec's `tap_requires: ["32/0"]` narrowing
select exactly them. `Pplus` 31/0 marks the two substrate-tie
rings, which sit outside every well -- that separation is what
`controls/adc_block.tie-wrong-implant.control.json` exploits to
prove the tie check could have failed.
substrate_tie_candidates: 2, metal1_bars: 1 per ring
The two contacted `Comp`/`Contact`/`Metal1` guard rings
`lib/geometry.py:draw_guard_ring` draws, one around the analog
core and one around the reserved digital region. Each ring's
`Metal1` is now ONE merged polygon -- a closed annulus. It used
to be four mutually disjoint bars, open at all four corners, so
strapping one bar would have strapped a quarter of a ring.
READ `metal1_bar_pairs_touching` WITH CARE: it is 0 in BOTH
states and cannot tell them apart -- with a single polygon there
are no pairs to touch. `metal1_bars` (4 -> 1) is the field that
discriminates, and it is the one the test pins.
metal1_label_texts: 2 per ring
Two rather than one because the two rings' `Metal1` and the bar
that straps them together are one merged island, so each ring's
region interacts with both `vss` label texts. That is the
correct reading: electrically there is one strapped structure,
not two independent ones. Before #356 this was 0 on both -- the
rings were drawn and reached no supply at all.
contact_min_dim_um / contact_max_dim_um: 0.22 / 0.22
Each ring's contacts are an array of exact 0.22 um squares (3276
cuts on the analog ring, 1006 on the digital one), which is what
gf180mcu's `CO.1` asks for. They used to be four long bars
(0.468 um x up to 596.698 um) that passed the curated deck's
`contact.width.1` -- a MINIMUM-width check whose own description
calls itself an approximation of CO.1's exact min AND max size
rule. Pinned here rather than left to DRC for exactly that
reason.
LAYER NUMBERS come from the same two cross-checked sources
adc_block.supply-spec.json's own `_comment` names: the installed PDK's
gf180mcu.lyp layer table and klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck.
